What is trad, or traditional, living? Yesterday, when I posted about 'trad thoughts' I honestly gave myself a lot more to think about than I realized. My original intention was to just post little things, helpful tips, recipes, how-to's, etc. However, the more I thought about it, the more I realized that I wanted to give/get more than JUST advice.

When I first started my trad journey (i.e. Getting married because of the military, or else my then boyfriend and I couldn't live together), i didn't really know what I was doing. I mean, I'd had some guidance from my own mother, who stayed home with us kids, till my youngest brother started school full time. She cooked, cleaned, sewed, and did all the other traditional things to care for her family, but overall, I was never actually TAUGHT how to care for a home, a family, children. My mom was not what one would call patient. So, i had to learn the hard way - through many, many, many failures. I also didn't have anyone to lean on, and no real friends to speak of (though I did meet a couple military wives with whom I'm still in touch with today).

So, with these posts, I'm hoping that we can all come together, and be those ladies from which the younger ones can ask advice, be the shoulder to cry on when you're having an absolute crap day, tell each other that 'no, you're NOT crazy' when you feel like a hot mess and nothing gets done (ask me about my day yesterday, with that one!), and to be those voices of reason when everything seems absolutely upside down.

I also want us to laugh at jokes, rejoice in each other's happy moments, or heck even laugh at our failures (speaking of which, I'll be baking a cake later this weekend, and let's just say that cakes are not my forte, lol).

When I went to nursing school, they had a saying that "Nurses are the only profession that eat their own young." Unfortunately, i see this SO much with women in society and I think that we (ESPECIALLY those of us in the traditional roles) can do so much to help build each other up, and show the world (even a little piece of our communities, or this little corner of the virtual world) that love and values are still a very real thing. It's my hope that through the advice, recipes, instruction, and glimpses into everyday living, that we can strengthen our families, and ourselves.

(I apologize for the book. I'm not planning on all my posts being this long. Also, I realize that for everything posted, there's ALWAYS exceptions - whatever they may be - and unless specified, it's going to be a generalization. At least, for me, it will be)
